PRIMARY.pick: NONE meets the founder's brief (recurring revenue that pays a salary inside 36 months). Best available: DD2 lifecycle-intel (C-80 anchor + C-29 NVM cross-reference + C-61 LTB sizer; SaaS only, with the C-86 index kept as an option)
PRIMARY.rationale: This is the highest-expected-value path left after 186 red-team objections, none refuted (05_REDTEAM.md Scoreboard). DD2 is the only survivor that is (a) pure software in the founder's skill set, (b) sold to a buyer they already understand (procurement at U.S. SMB hardware OEMs), (c) recurring, and (d) testable in 29 days for about $3k. Revised BASE (models/lifecycle-intel.py re-run, exit 0; 04_DEEPDIVES/lifecycle-intel.md §0 and §14.3): first revenue m6 (2027-05); ARR $69,915 at m18 and $149,629 at m36; breakeven with the founder unpaid at m17 (2028-04); cash low $6,100 at m16, a $33,900 draw; cash $76,410 at m36. GLUT gives $104,077 and SEVERE $83,031. The lifecycle module holds its revenue in the glut (+0%), while the price-alert module falls 57%. It never covers a $10k/month salary in any scenario. But it is the only survivor whose own model reaches full-time inside 36 months on a plausible upside: at 15% trial conversion (a strong K1 pass) it reaches $318,279 ARR at m36, covers the salary at m31 and goes full-time at m33. The threshold is ≥14.7% conversion or 1.51x the trial inflow. It beats DD5 for PRIMARY on four counts: it is mostly subscription (DD5 is 60-71% services); its ceiling is larger (3,000 U.S. SMB OEMs, where $1M ARR needs 7.9% penetration, against DD5's ~$0.42M/yr serviceable ceiling); it needs no exclusive memory contractor; and its test costs a third as much ($2,950 vs ~$9.1k). On the ceiling: the red team puts it at $0.1-0.3M ARR (RT-VC-DD2-04). This is a side business that might become a small company, not a venture. Confidence 0.2 = the probability it passes K0+K1+K6 on 2026-12-01 and reaches the m12 gate. I put ≤0.1 on it paying a salary inside 36 months.
PRIMARY.gate: K0 comes first: a written employer carve-out covering the product, the target industry and third-party PO contributions, signed before any code (target 2026-11-09). A refusal kills DD2 for this founder. By 2026-12-01, two gates, and either failing kills DD2: K6, 25 qualified calls booked within 21 days from cold outreach outside the employer's network; and K1, ≥5 of the 25 pay a refundable $500 deposit or sign a paid LOI at ≥$200/month. K5: Nexar or DigiKey grants in-app price display in writing at ≤$1,000/month by 2026-12-15; if not, re-test K1 on a demo built from public prints only. Later stops: fewer than 2 paying accounts by 2027-08-31 (m9); fewer than 5 accounts or MRR below $1,700 by 2027-11-30 (m12); cash below $5k in any month. Salary test: measured trial conversion of ≥14.7%.
PRIMARY.spend: $0 on code before K0. Between 2026-11-02 and 2026-12-01, ≤$2,950 (hard cap $5,000): ~$500 employment-agreement review, ~$100 Sales Navigator, ~$1,250 in $50 call thank-yous, ~$1,000 government-contracts attorney, ~$100 domain and hosting. If K0, K1 and K6 pass, release cash only as the model's path needs it. Beyond the test: ≤~$22k by m9 (2027-08) and ≤~$29k by m12 (2027-11). Never exceed the model's $33,900 maximum draw, and stop below $5k of cash.

FALLBACK.pick: DD5 open-memory-ip: C-33 OpenRAM macro service for sky130/GF180 open-PDK tapeouts (the wedge only; the T2 legs C-32 and C-22 are dead)
FALLBACK.rationale: This is the safest path to revenue left, and its risk does not move with DD2's. Its buyers are university, startup and SBIR tapeout teams, not SMB-OEM procurement, and open-silicon IP is unlikely to collide with a design/manufacturing employer. Revised BASE (models/open-memory-ip.py re-run, exit 0; 04_DEEPDIVES/open-memory-ip.md §14.3): 57% gross margin; cash-positive from m12 (2027-11); recurring ARR $41.2k at m18 and $65.7k at m36 ($164.1k run-rate including services); cash $88.4k at m36. It holds up best in a glut of all the survivors: GLUT m36 ARR is $54.9k (-16%) with $60.4k of cash. A $2.5k cash gate keeps the $40k from going negative (cash low $4.0k at m15), and a failed day-30 test loses about $9k. The limits are real. It never pays the founder in BASE, GLUT or SEVERE (peak GP $8.0k/month against the $11.85k needed). Its ceiling is ~$0.42M/yr, and a full free release by UCSC or OCD cuts m36 ARR to $34.0k. The founder cannot sign off the timing on what they sell, so a contract memory engineer under a 12-month exclusivity, or a technical cofounder, must be signed by m3. Net EV is +$5-15k over three years before counting the founder's time (research/phase5/responses_open-memory-ip.json ev_note). Confidence 0.2 = the deep-dive owner's 15-25% pass estimate for the strengthened day-30 test.
FALLBACK.gate: The day-30 test passes only if all four rules pass: (i) count interest only from distinct funded teams; (ii) ≥2 open-PDK commercial or SBIR LOIs of ≥$10k; (iii) contractor-signed extracted-SPICE corners plus a 1,000-point Monte Carlo on the ≥16 KB macro; (iv) written no-release statements from both UCSC VLSIDA and OCD, where silence counts as a FAIL. After that: an exclusive contract memory engineer or a technical cofounder signed by m3, and ≥1 university PO by m6. Drop DD5 on any failed rule.
FALLBACK.spend: $0 in November beyond the two test-(iv) emails sent on Monday. ≤$9.1k for the day-30 test, starting 2026-12-02 and only if DD2 fails K0, K1 or K6. If DD2 died on K0, first get a separate written carve-out for DD5. After a pass, one-time spends are gated by the model's $2.5k cash floor; expect to draw up to ~$36k of the $40k by m15.

MOONSHOT.pick: NONE honestly qualifies: no surviving, parked or reopenable path shows venture-scale math. Best available: C-86, a contract-reference Memory Cost Escalation Index (DD2's killed index leg), held as a ~$0 option inside the DD2 kill test
MOONSHOT.rationale: The ceiling survey: 03_SCORING.md §6 puts 11 of the top 15 concepts under $0.5M of year-5 ARR and none in the $2-10M band. The one path it found above $2M is C-86 becoming the reference index in contract language. Every other high-ceiling candidate fails worse. DD7 Plan B (C-65 hi-rel MCM + C-91 die bank) was the round-2 MOONSHOT candidate. It returns 0.29x of $11.49M in BASE. Even its BULL case (4 design-ins a year, year-10 revenue $26.48M) is 7.22x on $5.5M, about 21.9%/yr gross over 10 years before dilution: a private-equity return, not a venture one. It also needs OCM aftermarket rights (P ≤5%), a hi-rel cofounder and an MCM redesign (models/legacy-dram-diebank.py §6 and §10g). C-36 (Fab 25 SRAM second source; the best T2, moonshot rank #20) has founder-fit 1, needs 30-42 months to revenue and is a '$5-15M fight over a shrinking pie' against Infineon at the same fab. DD6 is an integrator for which $1M ARR is unreachable. C-86 is different in kind. A benchmark written into surcharge and EPA clauses is the only founder-reachable moat in the study that compounds and persists through the 2028 turn, at 85-91% GM, on ~$0 of capital. But the red team killed it as designed (RT-VC-DD2-01, FATAL). A SaaS-fed panel reaches only 14 of the 15 contributors it needs by m36. Even with 10 seed contributors the model publishes at m20 and sells 1.8 licences by m36. $1M ARR needs 115 licences at $8,700/yr against TrendForce contract prints and open-book pass-through, and DRAM has never had a working settlement index (SGX's 2003 DRAM futures failed; C-87). It qualifies as a MOONSHOT only if buyers sign contribution and citation paper by day 30. Confidence 0.03 that it passes K3+K4 and reaches an executed contract by m15; ≤0.01 that it reaches venture scale.
MOONSHOT.gate: By 2026-12-01, asked on the same DD2 calls: K3, ≥2 of 10 signed LOIs naming a live contract or surcharge schedule that would cite the index, each saying why TrendForce prints and open-book pass-through don't serve it; AND K4, ≥10 contribution agreements signed by each company's legal function, covering 24 months of line-item memory PO prices (each from a buyer with ≥$250k/yr of memory spend that is not EMS-turnkey), with ≥70% of spend in ≤4 grade-homogeneous cells and ≥3 of those cells able to reach 5 contributors. At m9 (2027-08-31): ≥3 cells with ≥5 independent buyers in ≥80% of quarters, and noise below one-third of the TrendForce move. The option closes for good at m15 (2028-02-29) unless the panel has ≥15 members or one executed contract between unaffiliated parties names the index. Venture-scale test: a credible path to ≥115 licences.
MOONSHOT.spend: $0 extra now. The K3/K4 asks ride on DD2's calls, and DD2's ~$1,000 attorney consult covers the DLAD and antitrust questions. Buy the $5k written antitrust opinion only after K3 and K4 pass. No outside raise and no full-time move until an executed contract between unaffiliated parties cites the index.

honest_framing: For a founder with under $50k, the study's answer to 'make RAM, or something better, in America' is no. The 2025-26 shortage is a price spike, not a cost opening. Incumbents make DDR5 at ~$1.48/GB and still earn ~82% gross margin at the $8.15/GB glut price, and no alternative memory comes within 10x of DDR5 on $/GB. The U.S. has no DRAM foundry, no display fab and no open die supply, and buyers pay no 'Made in USA' premium for memory: TAA treats Korean, Taiwanese and Japanese DRAM as equal, and the Section 232 rate on memory is 0% (01_LANDSCAPE.md §0). Every device or fab-adjacent path is T2+ with founder-fit 1. After 186 red-team objections with none refuted, all seven deep dives were killed or cut to side lines. The best survivor (DD2) reaches ~$150k ARR at m36 and never pays a salary in BASE, and no path shows venture math: the best modelled bull case, DD7 Plan B, is ~22%/yr gross before dilution on $5.5M. Re-aim the project. Drop 'make memory' as the mission, keep the day job, and use the shortage for one ~$3k, 30-day cash test of one software line sold to a buyer the founder already understands. Judge it only on paid deposits by 2026-12-01. If it fails, stop spending on memory, because the window closes with the 2028 price turn, and move the venture search to operations and supply-chain software for hardware makers, where the founder's build speed is the edge and capital and fab access are not needed (subject to the same employer carve-out).
biggest_unknown: Whether anyone pays. After seven phases no buyer has paid for or signed anything on any line, and every number rests on desk research and search snippets (01_LANDSCAPE.md evidence grade). The question that decides it: will U.S. SMB hardware OEM procurement put down cash for memory EOL/PCN/cost intelligence from a part-time vendor before the 2028 price turn removes the urgency? DD2's K1 tests this: ≥5 of 25 qualified calls give a refundable $500 deposit or a paid LOI at ≥$200/month. A salary needs conversion near ≥14.7%, against the 10% the model assumes. K0, the employer carve-out, is the precondition and can end it first.
monday_action: Monday 2026-11-02, about 110 minutes, $0 out of pocket. (1) 20 min: write DD2's K0-K6 pass/fail thresholds (04_DEEPDIVES/lifecycle-intel.md §10) plus the MOONSHOT K3/K4 bars into a dated document, and email it to one outside procurement advisor so the bars are locked before any call. (2) 60 min: pull the employment agreement and mark the IP-assignment, moonlighting and non-compete/non-solicit clauses. Book the ~$500 attorney review. Draft the written carve-out request: product = memory lifecycle and cost SaaS; industry = U.S. SMB hardware OEMs; it also covers third-party PO-price contributions. No code until it is signed. (3) 30 min: send three emails. To Nexar (support@nexar.com) and DigiKey's API team: may a third-party SaaS display your prices and stock in-app, and at what monthly cost (K5)? To UCSC VLSIDA and OCD: do you plan free ≥16 KB sky130/GF180 SRAM macro releases, answer in writing (DD5 test iv)?

watch_list.trigger: $0 watch: the final FAR rule in FAR Case 2023-008 (§5949; proposed 2026-02-17; prohibition from 2027-12-23) is published and removes or narrows reliance on supplier certification after 'reasonable inquiry', or requires third-party or die-level verification of DRAM. Alternatively, the optional $1.4k Stage-1 probe finds a module maker that pays cash and states in writing that it cannot get die-source declarations. Even then the modelled best case is $226,833 ARR at m36, so reopen it as a side line unless the rule mandates third-party verification.

$0 watch; both are needed. (a) A VAR or MSP commits in writing to ≥6 boxes/yr on its own paper at ≤15%/20%. (b) Either a published or socket-pinned single-socket run shows ≥10 tok/s per user at 4 concurrent users on a 1T-class MoE in a box quoting ≤$65k (e.g. a next-generation MRDIMM platform), or a blind evaluation shows regulated buyers clearly prefer 200B-1T models over single-GPU 30-120B models. This is the most mission-aligned trigger ('DRAM doing HBM's job'). Check server-platform launches and public open-source hybrid-inference benchmarks once a quarter.

$0 watch: a hi-rel co-founder brings an existing x72 design-in plus ≥3 evaluation LOIs at ≥$1,200/unit, with a stacked/RDL layout that fits the package and a 125 °C retention-bin plan. This is the study's highest modelled ceiling (BULL year-10 revenue $26.48M), but it needs $5.5-11.5M; reopen it only as a co-founder-led T2 raise.

$0 watch: a written OCM offer of authorized-aftermarket rights (wafers, test programs and marking) for a named EOL DRAM part, together with an all-in pull cost of ≤$1.53/die (the IRR break-even). The owner put P(rights within 15 months) at ≤5%.

A $1.2k, 28-day demand-only probe, run only with spare hours. It reopens on ≥30 full-list deposits (at most one-third from i-series owners) plus a reseller LOI for ≥100 cards/yr, or on a white-label commitment of ≥200 cards/yr for 2 years. The SAM is ~$0.62M/yr, so this is side income at most.

rejected: DD6 private MoE appliance (C-48) as PRIMARY: KILLED. BASE m36 ARR is $63,873, the 36-month net is -$29,411, a $25k bridge is needed and the founder is never full-time; full-time needs a 21% close rate (04_DEEPDIVES/private-moe-appliance.md §14.2).

DD7 Plan B (C-65 + C-91) as MOONSHOT: 0.29x of $11.49M in BASE; BULL is 7.22x on $5.5M, ≈22%/yr gross before dilution; it needs OCM rights (≤5%), a hi-rel cofounder and an MCM redesign; founder-fit 1.

C-36 SkyWater Fab 25 SRAM second source as MOONSHOT: never deep-dived, but founder-fit is 1, revenue takes 30-42 months, Infineon anchors the same fab, and outside access to the SRAM bitcell/PDK is unverified.
DD1 provenance-recert (C-64/C-62) as FALLBACK: KILLED. Recert earns -$3/module, CleanBOM reaches $58,335 ARR at m36, and module makers can self-certify for free.
DD3 NV continuity cards (C-12) as FALLBACK: KILLED. BASE 36-month net is -$29.8k, peak cash need is $49.2k (> $40k), and breakeven needs 33 cards/month.
DD4 memory efficiency (C-73/C-74/C-75): KILLED. The fee is $1.66/node/month against $2.9-3.4k/month of on-call plus E&O, and cash goes below $0 at M12.

DD5's T2 legs (C-32 Si gain cell, C-22 ReRAM chiplet) as a 'made in America memory' moonshot: KILLED. A logic-rule gain cell does not beat the pushed-rule 6T on sky130, there is no leakage case at 130 nm, ReRAM's magnet axis is shared by OTP/eFuse, and there is no named buyer.
C-13 emerging-memory test lab: 10-30 U.S. customers, and its value rests on a reliability-physicist hire the founder cannot be.
C-18 NewSpace MRAM rad-data service: Teledyne HiRel became Everspin's authorized screening channel (2026-09-02), NASA data is free, and ECCN 3A001 adds an export gate.
C-92 AS6171 counterfeit lab: ~$650k, underwater below 36 lots/month, and SMT Corp and Micross are already accredited nearby.
C-79 TB-RAM rental: DDR4 bought at peak prices must pay back before end-2027, on-call clashes with the day job, and 10 boxes earn ~$0.14M/yr.
C-84 RAM-diet profiler: one-off $5-20k audits that engineers can do free; the saving is ~$2.5/unit at glut prices.

C-45 KV Pool Node, C-49 CXL node, C-37 GSI APU appliance, C-55 analog-CIM module, C-67 rugged CAMM2: 15-30% integrator margins against vendors that already sell the same box (Penguin MemoryAI, Dell/HPE/Supermicro, GSI, Mythic/EnCharge, Innodisk/Virtium).

Any U.S. fab, trailing-node DRAM or alternative-memory device play: there is no host fab and no open die, nothing comes within 10x of DDR5 on $/GB, and every T3/T4 concept was killed (01_LANDSCAPE.md §0).
Running DD2 and DD5 in parallel from day 1: ~15 h/week cannot staff both. DD7's model showed that diverting 10 h/month pushed DD6's Phase-4 full-time month from m23 to m33.
Raising outside money now for any path: every VC verdict reads lifestyle or side business, and no path has venture math to show an investor.
C-87 DRAM futures/swaps as the index's scale-up: R1-UNSUPPORTED. SGX's 2003 DRAM futures and the CBOT/NYMEX studies produced no market.

A generic (non-memory) component-lifecycle SaaS as PRIMARY now: not modelled in this study, and SiliconExpert, Octopart/Nexar and Z2Data hold that ground. Consider it only as the re-aim direction after DD2's K1 data is in.
